newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia dlr subdued but market too short to sell.
newsitem.headline: Australia dlr subdued but market too short to sell.

text.p: The Australian dollar hung around in a tight range at midday as flows of funds and news dried up.

Traders said market sentiment remained decidedly chilly toward the currency as reflected in the weight of U.S. and European bank selling at US$0.7530 overnight, which snuffed out a modest rally. Nevertheless, after weeks of such sales much of the market was very short of the dollar and even the rumour of bids beneath US$0.7480 was enough to discourage further offers, as least for the moment.
A recovery looked remote, however, given the market saw an RBA rate cut approaching in a cloud of dust on the horizon.
By 12.00 pm (0200 GMT) the local dollar had settled at US$0.7490/95, up from an early US$0.7475 low but off Wednesday's late US$0.7515/20.

The currency was just as subdued on the crosses, taking its cue from US$/yen which had turned quiet ahead of the weekend G7 meeting, idling at 84.93/03 yen from an early 84.90/00 and 85.27/37. It was unchanged in trade weighted terms at 56.9.
The only data today were merchandise imports for May which are little watched since they are not seasonally adjusted nor on a balance of payments basis like current account fgiures.
